alternatives.option: General runtime type coercion via `Convert.ChangeType` or provider-level implicit conversions.
alternatives.whyRejected: Conceals schema drift and precision loss, introduces conversions outside an explicit supported matrix, and incurs per-value runtime conversion overhead.

alternatives.option: Strict column/parameter presence, failing when a mapped column or output parameter is absent from a query result.
alternatives.whyRejected: Prevents reusing a single model class across queries that return different subsets of columns.

alternatives.option: Require consumers to expose signed-integer or `byte[]` surrogate properties on models instead of supporting unsigned and `sbyte` types on mapping attributes.
alternatives.whyRejected: Forces boilerplate conversion properties into domain models despite attribute-driven storage representation selection.

alternatives.option: Platform-endian binary encoding for numeric binary mappings.
alternatives.whyRejected: Makes persisted `binary`/`varbinary` representations dependent on machine endianness and breaks unsigned byte-order sorting on little-endian hosts.

fields.consequences: Undeclared CLR/database type pairings fail immediately during mapping construction (`InvalidMapTypeException`), while models remain reusable across queries returning partial column sets. For SQL Server numeric binary mappings (`[MapToSqlBinary]`, `[MapToSqlVarBinary]`), invalid configured attribute lengths throw `InvalidBinaryMappingLengthException` during mapping validation (`IsValidType`), and non-null payloads whose runtime byte length differs from the target type's byte width throw `InvalidBinaryValueLengthException` during reader or output-parameter decoding. Fixed-width big-endian `binary(n)` and equal-width `varbinary` payloads preserve true unsigned sort order for `ulong`, `uint`, and `ushort` under SQL Server byte-by-byte comparison (matching same-width SQL integer `CAST` representations), whereas signed integer mappings do not preserve unsigned sort order and neither `tinyint` nor `binary(1)` preserves signed `sbyte` sort order. `ShardKey` binary/external serialization does not include `ulong`, `uint`, `ushort`, or `sbyte`.
fields.context: Silent runtime type coercions hide precision and schema-mismatch bugs and add per-row overhead, whereas strict compile/build-time validation of attribute-to-property pairings catches mismatches early. At the same time, domain models legitimately use `enum` types, unsigned integers (`ulong`, `uint`, `ushort`), and signed bytes (`sbyte`), and a single model class is routinely reused across queries that return different column subsets (such as summary vs. detail queries). For unsigned integers stored in SQL Server, fixed-width big-endian binary encoding (`binary(8/4/2)`) preserves unsigned sort order under SQL Server's byte-by-byte binary comparison, while same-width integer storage (`bigint`/`int`/`smallint`/`tinyint`) provides compact integer storage when unsigned SQL ordering is not required.
fields.decision:
Mapping attributes declare a closed set of supported CLR-to-database representations and reject undeclared pairings when constructing the mapping delegate, while tolerating missing result columns and missing output parameters at execution time (logging at `Debug` level and resolving column ordinals once per result set). In `ArgentSea.Sql`:
1. `MapToSqlBigInt`, `MapToSqlInt`, `MapToSqlSmallInt`, and `MapToSqlTinyInt` permit explicit reversible same-width unchecked conversions for `ulong` (`bigint`), `uint` (`int`), `ushort` (`smallint`), and `sbyte` (`tinyint`), including nullable forms.
2. `MapToSqlBinary` and `MapToSqlVarBinary` permit fixed-width big-endian binary encoding (`8`, `4`, `2`, and `1` bytes) for `ulong`, `uint`, `ushort`, and `sbyte` (and nullable forms) across input parameters, output parameters, data readers, and table-valued parameters.
3. For enum properties, `MapToSqlInt`, `MapToSqlSmallInt`, and `MapToSqlTinyInt` accept any enum or `Nullable<enum>` regardless of the enum's underlying integer width, while `MapToSqlBigInt` accepts any non-nullable enum and rejects `Nullable<enum>`.
fields.title: Permit explicit reversible storage representations while rejecting implicit coercion
